topic: Six Kingdom and Three Domain Classification Systems
key_concepts: Organisms are classified using hierarchical taxonomic levels from kingdom to species
Scientific names identify organisms within the taxonomic hierarchy
The six-kingdom system includes Plantae, Protista, Eubacteria, Fungi, Animalia, and Archae
Organisms are classified by cell type as prokaryotic or eukaryotic
Organisms are classified by number of cells as unicellular or multicellular
Cell wall, cell membrane, and chloroplast are structural features used in classification
Modes of nutrition include ingestion, photosynthesis, and absorption
Kingdom Plantae organisms obtain nutrition through photosynthesis
Fungi differ from plants in their structural features
The three-domain system groups life into Bacteria, Archaea, and Eukarya
Domains differ in cellular structures, habitat, and scientific names
